utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And could we have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and Kimberly Fleming, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. And the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Alexis Demirdjian, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone in the courtroom, the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom. I'm going to ask Mr. Registrar to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing will commence. We were informed yesterday evening that there are three witnesses scheduled for today. Could the Prosecution inform us of the order in which the witnesses will be appearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's correct, there are three witnesses available today. In respect to the order, can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Withopf. We will go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not quite. I can't see the symbol on my screen -- oh, there is it is. We are in open session. You want to tender two cassettes into evidence. As far as I can remember, that is a witness who was granted protective measures, so we have to go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. Zivko Totic didn't request any protective measures. He testified in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So please produce the two cassettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, it was the video footage shown to the witness Zivko Totic. We were able to isolate it. It has been burned on one CD. Both portions are on the one CD, and the nine copies can be made available to the parties. The last time Defence insisted -- insisted repeatedly -- that the Prosecution should play the video footage again. We are well prepared to do the same exercise today again. It's only five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am turning to the Defence. The Prosecution, in accordance with your request, would like to have these sequences shown, because on these cassettes we have in fact two videos. Mr. Bourgon, there are no objections to having these two sequences viewed?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the technical booth please take the necessary steps to show the sequences. In theory, we should see these two videos on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence doesn't object to having this admitted into evidence immediately, without viewing them again. This is just to save time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber would like to thank the Defence for trying to save time. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for this cassette that in fact consists of two sequences.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the exhibit number will be P69 and P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the number will be P69 and P70. Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll now commence the hearing of the witness, Mr. Dragan Radic. Could the usher go and call the witness into the courtroom. Could the usher go and call the witness into the courtroom. [The witness entered court]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Dragan Radic. Are you receiving the interpretation of what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you have been called here as a witness, given that you have to make a solemn declaration, could you tell me what your first and last name is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Radic. I'm from Guca Gora, near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth and what is your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 5th of November, 1963, in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are you by profession at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a technician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, over ten years ago, what was your profession at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was also a medical technician at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Have you already testified before court, either before a national court or international court, or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As you will be testifying before a court, you have to make a solemn declaration. Could you please read the text that the usher will show you in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll provide you with some explanations as to the procedure that will be followed here. You will have to answer the questions put to you by the representatives of the Prosecution, who are to your right. One of the two persons who are to your right will be examining you on the basis of the documents that concern the witnesses. An hour and a half has been allocated for your examination. After the Prosecution has concluded its examination-in-chief, the representatives of the Defence will conduct their cross-examination and will be putting questions to you in order to verify that you are a credible witness. And in addition, they will be asking you questions that are relevant for the defence of the accused. The Judges, who are sitting before you, may at any point in time, if they consider it necessary, ask you questions in order to clarify issues that you may have addressed when answering the questions put to you by the Prosecution. This depends on how you answer the questions put to you. To the extent that this is possible, try to answer the questions fully and precisely, because your oral testimony will serve to establish the truth for the Judges who are before you. And your oral testimony, which will be supported by documents that the Prosecution will be tendering into evidence, will be the base on which we will attempt to establish the probative value of your testimony. As you have made a solemn declaration, it is your duty to tell the truth. If you give false testimony, a witness could be punished and the penalties could be either a seven-year prison sentence or a fine. But as you have made the solemn declaration, this is a possibility that we exclude. In addition, when answering the questions put to you, you might feel that some of the information you have to provide could be used against you at a subsequent date. In such a case, you can say that you don't want to answer the question. If the Trial Chamber forces you to answer the question, at that point the Trial Chamber would inform you that given the Rules of Procedure and Evidence the information you provide can't be used against you. If you feel that there are any difficulties, please inform us of the difficulties, and we will address the issue. Have you understood what I have said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having listened to us. I'll now turn to the Prosecution. I think it is Mr. Withopf who will be conducting the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Mr. President. Indeed, it's me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: My apologies. Examined by Mr. Withopf:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you just informed the Trial Chamber that you were born in Guca Gora. Could you please also tell the Trial Chamber where you grew up.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I grew up in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you live in 1992 and early 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, have you ever been a member of the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber when you joined the JNA and when you left the JNA.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I went to the JNA in 1985, and I served until 1986.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Radic, when you joined the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Trial Chamber when you joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, 1992, I became a member of the HVO, and I took a solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber, Mr. Radic, which unit, which military unit of the HVO you joined in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was the Travnik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you joined the HVO, the Travnik Brigade, what were your duties within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was in charge of setting up a medical corps in the area of Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the HVO unit in the area of Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: In the area of Guca Gora, a battalion was set up which belonged to the Travnik Brigade up to the 1st of April, 1993, and that was when the Frankopan Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Frankopan Brigade have a command post in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber from when and until when.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was established on the 1st of April, 1993, and it existed up to the end of May 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber where exactly this command post was established in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The command post of the Frankopan Brigade was in the old house which was part of the monastery in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away, to your knowledge, was this old house which you described being part of the monastery in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: You mean from the monastery?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was part of the monastery, but we used to call it "the old house" because it was in a rather dilapidated state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe, Mr. Radic, the relationship between the Muslim and the Croat population in the area of Guca Gora in early 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was peaceful, up to the arrival of refugees from Krajina, Jajce, Karaula. There were no tensions before that, up to the moment of their arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did happen, Mr. Radic, at the moment of their arrival?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: When people from Krajina arrived in the area of the villages around Guca Gora -- Mosor, Krpeljici, Radojcici, Maljine -- the structure of the population changed, the make-up of the population changed. All of a sudden they started putting barricades on the roads, they started establishing checkpoints. People were stopped and searched at the checkpoints. I'm talking about the local population that had used to move around without any problems before that. There were minor provocations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background, Mr. Radic, of the people who came from the areas of Krajina, Jajce, and Karaula?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Mr. Radic, when a real conflict broke out between the Muslims and the Croats in the area of Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: You're asking me about the period when that happened?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Did there come a time when an actual war broke out between the HVO and the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: At the moment when they arrived, there was already something in the air. There were tensions in the air. There was fear among the local Muslim and local Croat population. There was the feeling of distrust amongst both. Nobody even thought about any conflicts. There was nothing being said about any possible conflicts that might happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Guca Gora was attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the end of April, there was shooting by Muslims from Radojcici. We didn't know in Guca Gora what was going on. We only heard shots from Radojcici. They were shooting from Radojcici towards us. And also, towards the end of April there was shooting from Donje Maljine, also by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did there come a second time, Mr. Radic, when Guca Gora was attacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Guca Gora was attacked on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber which army attacked Guca Gora on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: 306th Mountain Brigade and the 7th Muslim. And according to our information, those were units of the 3rd Corps at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps of which army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Of the Bosniak army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber how you got to know that it was the 306th Mountain Brigade and the 7th Muslim Brigade which were involved in the attack on Guca Gora on 8 June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: We learned that from the local Muslims, who had told us that the 7th Muslim was being formed in Zenica and that members of the 7th Muslim were predominantly Mujahedins. A lot of people, a lot of foreigners passed through our village; that is, Mujahedins passed through our village. And we learned, when Guca Gora fell, from our civilians who were captured and taken to Maljine and Mehurici -- a few days later they were exchanged and we received information from them that it was that unit that was involved in the attack. And also, on the radio station of Travnik Nadja Ridzic praised the successes of the BH army, the 7th Muslim, and the 306th Mountain Brigade. She said that the extremists from the ranks of the HVO had been chased away from Guca Gora and the neighbouring villages. And she also said that this area should have surrendered to the BH army. This is what we heard on Radio Travnik when they were expelled to Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who this person, Nadja Ridzic is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: She is a journalist. She's affiliated with Radio Travnik and also with Television Travnik. At that time, she used to call us Croats extremists and Ustasha. She would use those words on her radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radic, you explained how you got to know about the 7th Muslim Brigade. Can you please also explain to the Trial Chamber what prompted you to know that it was the 306th Mountain Brigade which was involved in the attack on -- at Guca Gora on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The 306th --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 14:24, the Prosecution has repeated the same question and the witness has already answered that question. So I don't see the reason for putting the same question to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm happy to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please; rephrase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, in addition to the reasons you just explained to the Trial Chamber as to how you got to know that the 7th Muslim Brigade and the 306th Mountain Brigade were involved in the attack at Guca Gora, was there anything in particular, in addition, which prompted you to get to know that the 306th Mountain Brigade was involved in that attack?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The 306th Mountain Brigade was stationed in Rudnik. I went there on several occasions. I went to the command, and I also went there when I was passing through the village of Karlovcic when I was taking the wounded and the sick towards the Nova Bila hospital. And before the conflict, I also learned from the local Muslims that this 7th Muslim Brigade had been established in Zenica, that its members were predominantly foreign citizens, Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, what were your duties during the attack on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the medical unit of the Frankopan Brigade. My duty was to set up this medical unit in the area of Guca Gora and the neighbouring villages. I was also in charge of setting up field hospitals to provide them with drugs, stretchers, and other equipment. And also, if I had a vehicle at my disposal, I was in charge of transforming it for the purposes of serving the medical unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of the attack, was there any communication between the HVO and the ABiH for the purpose to exchange the wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were personal contacts. We would get in touch over the telephone with the command of the 306th Mountain Brigade in Rudnik and in Bila. And over the telephone we would agree. And then I could pass towards Brajkovici, Cukle with the ambulance in order to pull out the wounded and the sick from those villages. Whenever I arrived in any of these villages, I had to pass by the headquarters of the brigade, and then both I and the vehicle would be searched. Then I would be allowed to proceed towards Grahovcici, Brajkovici. It depended on where I was headed, in order to pull out the wounded. Dr. Suad Trkic participated in those negotiations. He was deployed in Rudnik on behalf of the BH army. On several occasions, I spoke to him and we said to each other that we were both medical personnel and that we had to do our job. And when it comes to the wounded and the injured, it sufficed for me to call him and I would be given a free passage; and vice versa, the same arrangement would be provided for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The command of the 306th Mountain Brigade, who actually was the commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I know that his family name was Sipic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The headquarters of the 306th Mountain Brigade in Rudnik and Bila, how far away is Rudnik from Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: 4 or 4 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of the attack of the ABiH 3rd Corps 306th Mountain Brigade and the 7th Muslim Brigade, Mr. Radic, what happened to the command post of the Jure Frankopan Brigade, close to the monastery you were talking about earlier on today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has also not understood the question. The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not raising the question of whether the witness has understood the question. I would only like to draw your attention that the witness has never told us that the command post of the Jure Francetic Brigade [sic] was in the vicinity of the monastery. He said that it was in the old house which was an integral part of the monastery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the Prosecution should rephrase the question and be more precise, because the question was rather ambiguous, Mr. Withopf. And the witness has never said that the command post of the Frankopan Brigade was in the vicinity of the monastery. So you may wish to clarify that as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, as a result of the ABiH attack on 8th June 1993, what happened to the command post of the HVO in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, the command post of the Frankopan Brigade was not in Guca Gora. Towards the end of May, it was relocated to Nova Bila. So on the 8th of June, there was just a communications man in the old house where the command post used to be, and there was also an operations man, a local of Guca Gora who used to live there. So on the 8th of June, the command post of this brigade was no longer in the old house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, just for clarification, earlier on today you said that from the 1st of April, 1993, to the 30th of May, 1994, there was the command post of the Jure Francetic -- of the Frankopan Brigade in Guca Gora. Was it just a mistake on your side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: From the 1st of April until the end of May 1993, not 1994. It was up to the end of May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radic, for this clarification. Does this mean that on the 8th of June, 1993, there was no command post of the Frankopan Brigade in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Towards the end of May, between the 25th and the 26th of May, 1993, the command post was moved to Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radic. Can you please very briefly describe for the Trial Chamber the cause of the attack at Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the BH army sent most of its troops from Turbe via Guca Gora, so all the members moving from Zevica [phoen] towards Turbe, to the front line facing the Serbs, had to pass via Guca Gora. And I suppose that they were bothered by being constantly controlled by the locals who carried arms in their own villages and were afraid of this constant passage of the large number of troops through Guca Gora. And I suppose that this was one of the major reasons why Guca Gora and the neighbouring villages were attacked. They wanted to improve their communication between Travnik and Zenica. They wanted to get a free passage through there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber whether the ABiH was successful in attacking Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was successful for them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did it mean for you on the 8th of June, 1993? Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: This meant that I was expelled from my place of birth, from my house. We had to leave all of our possessions behind. We had to seek refuge. We withdrew towards Nova Bila. At first we thought we would go as far as Sarici. This is a village 2 kilometres away from Guca Gora. However, we were not left in peace there. We were expelled from there towards Cifluk and Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, did you stay in the village of Cifluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Cifluk, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you stay in the village of Cifluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: From the 8th of June, until when I was wounded, on the 24th of December, 1993, when I was transferred to the hospital in Nova Bila. And on the 12th of January, 1994, I was taken to Split for medical treatment. I was taken there by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When on the 8th of June, 1993 did you arrive in Cifluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: We arrived at about 10.00 or half past 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far away is the village of Cifluk from Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Between 3 and 3 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your permission, I'm now going to show the witness Radic a map using the Sanction technology but also using the hard copies, which are available for distribution. This map, for the information of both Defence counsel and the Trial Chamber, is a part, is a portion of the bigger map which was admitted into evidence as Prosecution Exhibit P1 at the very beginning of this trial. Can the witness please be given one copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, can you identify on the map in front of you the villages of Guca Gora and the villages of Cifluk.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Guca Gora --

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can the witness be -- can the witness please be provided with a fine-liner.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Should I encircle it or ...?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. Radic. Can you please encircle the village of Guca Gora and the village of Cifluk.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please write next to Guca Gora "1" and next to Cifluk "2."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Radic. Can you please date and sign this map. Today is the 26th of February.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The usher will show the map to the Prosecution, to the Defence, and to the accused. Could we have an exhibit number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the exhibit number will be P72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radic. Once you arrived in Cifluk on the 8th of June, 1993 and onwards, did you monitor what was going on in Guca Gora? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, every day; with the naked eye and by using binoculars too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber what you have seen going on in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From 8th of June, 1993 onwards, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, when we arrived in Cifluk, part of the villagers withdrew with the troops, with people who were under arms, and with civilians, who were in their shelter. The other inhabitants of the village of Glavice remained at their positions because they didn't know that the other part of the village had withdrawn, as we had no contact with them. Upon arriving in Cifluk, we found out that there was more shooting. We heard this from Glavice and Krpeljici. And we realised that part of the village had remained in Guca Gora. They were at the entrance to Guca Gora, at the crossroads to Krpeljici and Guca Gora. Upon arriving in Cifluk, HVO members who were armed remained there and started digging in to prepare for defence in that area. We would take the civilians on foot to Nova Bila, because it was safer there. On that day, they kept shooting from the direction of Kljaci, Han Bila, Zolot [phoen], Hali Hodza [phoen]. They opened fire at the people there incessantly. From Sarici towards Cifluk. From Guca Gora to Sarici, the passage from Guca Gora to Sarici, on that way we had a blockade by the road. And above the road, 20 metres above the road, BH army trenches had been dug. This was a clear area. In order to take the civilians out, we had to attack those trenches and drive away the BH army troops from those trenches. There were local people from the village of Radojcici. When we managed to drive them away, we took the people to Sarici. In Sarici, which is a small village, everything was in an open space, fire was opened from all directions and they fired at the people and the troops. When we managed to get the people out of Sarici, we took them to Cifluk. As I have already said, the troops remained there. They dug in, because of -- the command of the Frankopan Brigade went there and stopped the army. They said we didn't have anywhere further to go. We had to return there. People understood this and assigned us the task of digging in. We would make dugouts. We felled timber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, may I please stop you here. On the 12th of June, 1993, did you watch what was going on in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what you have seen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of June, through the binoculars I saw houses burning in Guca Gora and stables as well. You could see this with the naked eye too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else have you seen happening in Guca Gora, other than burning houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I saw looting through the binoculars. I saw looting in the village. I saw how carts and tractors from the direction of Krpeljici and Maljine entered Guca Gora, descended towards our houses, loaded -- loaded things, and went towards Krpeljici or Maljine. There probably wasn't enough fuel at the time, so the tractors and the trailers would be parked before our convent in Guca Gora, at the Parace area and the Klisa area. And through binoculars, we were able to see how they were taking things out to Parace and Klisa, because it wasn't very far. You could see this very clearly through binoculars. We saw people in uniforms. We saw women wearing baggy Muslim trousers. We could more or less recognise whether a person was a woman or a man by looking at them through the binoculars. So they loaded these things on, and then the tractor or trailer would go towards Maljine or towards Krpeljici. Also, there is a residential building in Guca Gora. We saw a refrigerator lorry that came from Maljine and parked in front of the building. And they were also taking out furniture from that building and putting it in that lorry. Once they had done this, they went to the school to turn around there, the school in Guca Gora. Then they would come back through the village, pass by the monastery in the direction of Maljine. And I don't know where it finally went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, you were mentioning that furniture was taken out and you were repeatedly making reference to things that were taken out. Can you please be a bit more specific in respect to the things that were taken out.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, below the church, in the lower part of the village, Donja Mahala, as it is called, the two of us, I and Zorica Volic [phoen], would often look through the binoculars. And we saw two people carrying something, either a fridge or something else. It was something big, white. Sometimes it was black, too. And they were taking it towards Parace. They would leave it there and then return. And they did the same in Klisa above my house. I also saw two persons carrying something and then loading this into a trailer or a tractor. It depended on what they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furniture and a fridge. Is there anything else you became aware of that was taken away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, mostly bulky things we could see. One person may not have been able to carry this, a fridge or a large piece of furniture. They needed two persons to carry this. We had a big television in the house too. So most of the appliances, the technical appliances that they could carry out, they took these things out. Two persons would carry these things out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were mentioning earlier on that you have seen individuals in uniforms taking such things you just detailed away. Were these military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge and from what you have seen, soldiers of which military units were in Guca Gora on the 12th and the 13th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Guca Gora on the 8th of June was abandoned, and on the 9th of June there was still no one there, maybe four or five old people who couldn't move. Only local people from Krpeljici and Maljine could have done this, people who were members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were saying, Mr. Radic, that you watched what was going on in Guca Gora by using binoculars. The 12th and the 13th of June, 1993, how were the conditions, in terms of weather and having a clear sight?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was summer. It was clear. There wasn't a cloud anywhere. It was sunny. The weather was ideal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described the looting to some extent. From what you have seen, Mr. Radic, was there a certain system in place to loot the houses in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The village was deserted. There was no one there. They probably knew about this. They had done this -- they had worked together in fields for years. People would socialise. On the whole, people knew what others had in their houses. For example, a friend of mine with whom I played football for years in Guca Gora, Rasid Dautovic, who was a member of the BH army - he worked there as a communications officer - we spoke to each other over the radio and he told me that he had been in my room. He knew the layout of my room. He said he had taken some rings of mine, some golden chains, a light-blue trainer suit that he described in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This person with the name Rasid Dautovic whom you describe having been a member of the ABiH, do you know which unit he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was a BH army member in the village of Maljine before the conflict, a member of his unit in the village. And when we had been expelled from Guca Gora, when we received radio signals from Guca Gora, we recognised Rasid Dautovic's voice. He was personally asking a communications officer to ask how I was, to ask whether I was alive and well. This communications officer contacted me, and we spoke to each other over the officer and he told me about everything that I have just informed you of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, what unit did he belong to? What unit of the ABiH, if you know, Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: He was part of the communications unit which was located in the church in Guca Gora, because we received information according to which in Guca Gora - and this was through our intelligence service in the unit - we discovered that in the monastery in Guca Gora that is where the communications centre of the BH army was located. He was a communications officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This communication unit, was it established after the attack on the 8th of June, 1993, at Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, each village had its radio transmitter, and they communicated by using this means. So each village had a radio transmitter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having seen the looting in Guca Gora on the 12th and the 13th of June, 1993, did you get the impression that the items which were taken away were brought to a collection point?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've been following our learned colleague's examination-in-chief, and this is certainly the best way. It's how we all decide to examine witnesses. But from the beginning, the witness has been asked about the conclusion he drew as to when the communications centre was founded and as to whether after he had left Guca Gora and so on. The witness should tell us about this of his own accord. We now object to this last question because we see that the witness is asked to tell us about his impressions. We think that there are no grounds to ask the witness to address the Trial Chamber and talk to the Trial Chamber about his impressions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf, you've taken note of what the Defence has said. You're asking the witness to inform us of his impressions, not of what he may have seen or heard. And what he says would only be hearsay, so the value of such information is questionable then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen, Mr. Radic, after the items you detailed earlier on today were taken out from the houses, whether they were taken to certain areas in Guca Gora prior to being driven away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned the things that were taken out of the houses. I mentioned Parace, below the church, and Klisa, below my house. So what they took out they'd leave up there and then return to our houses down below. So if they took something out in Parace, it was left at Parace. They'd go and get other things, take them out again. When they had gathered enough things, they'd load them into the trailer or onto the tractor and go either to Maljine or to Krpeljici. So everything that they took out, if a tractor couldn't get to the house or if the trailer couldn't get there, they'd take them all out there, to Klisa and to Parace. I saw this through my binoculars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier on today, Mr. Radic, you already mentioned that there were also houses burning in Guca Gora. Can you please inform the Trial Chamber what you have seen in that respect.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, which is when Guca Gora fell, we were getting the wounded out throughout the day. Just before night fell, we saw tall flames in the vicinity of the church. We knew Guca Gora very well, so we knew that Danica Lujanovic's house was on fire. Half an hour later, the flames spread to the house below Danica's house, Lujanovic's house. Ivka and Niko Neimarevic's house. So it was before that day just before night fell. The third house which was burning was Nikola Markovic's house, our company commander. All the other houses were set on fire two or three days after Guca Gora had fallen. Two or three days after Guca Gora had fallen, they set fire to Jakica Rajic's house and his stable, Tomislav Rajic's house and his stable was set on fire. Afterwards, they went to the village and the late Stipe Rajic's house was set on fire. During the day, houses also burnt, and mostly houses burnt after unsuccessful attacks against our positions. And we knew that they would take revenge against the village, and this happened quite frequently. When they set fire to houses in the evening, the houses would have burnt down by dawn. But very often there were two or three houses burning during the night. And this was mostly from the 12th or 13th of June onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would suggest to make the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have our 25-minute break and we'll resume at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, before the break, you were informing the Trial Chamber in detail which houses were burnt down in Guca Gora on the 8th of June, 1993 and two or three days later. To your knowledge and based on from what you have seen, how many houses were burnt down in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Until the moment I was wounded on the 24th of December, 1993, approximately 50 houses were burnt and destroyed, 50 houses and cow sheds and stables.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge and from what you have seen, how many houses were destroyed within a week or two after the attack on 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: From the moment of the attack on the 8th of June, up to the 25th of June, approximately 15 to 20 houses and stables were burnt. So this was within this first period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were making a number of times, Mr. Radic, reference that "they were burning down houses." Whom are you actually referring to in saying "they"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: To the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Both civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to Muslim civilians and soldiers burning down houses, was anything else done for the purpose to destroy houses you became aware of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: We could see tiles being removed from the roofs of the houses in Donje Maljine, in the lowers part of the village. In the house of Anto Volic [phoen], we saw tiles being removed from the house. It was one of the better houses. The owner worked in Germany. And as we were watching, we could also see windows and doors being removed from the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the first weeks after the attack on the 8th of June, 1993, were there any inhabitants left in Guca Gora?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Only four or five bedridden elderly persons remained in Guca Gora. They couldn't leave their houses. According to information I received from people after the war, our Croats who remained in Travnik in their apartments and houses helped them. They would go to Guca Gora to see what had happened to their family houses, and they would bring food to these elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber what happened to your own house.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: My house was set on fire on the day when I was wounded, on the 24th of December, 1993. And it burnt to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your permission, I'm now going to show the witness a photograph in using both the Sanction technology and the hard copies that will be made available. For the information of the Trial Chamber and Defence counsel, this is a photograph which was taken in the course of the investigation against the accused Hadzihasanovic and Kubura in 2002. Can the photograph please be put on the ELMO and can the witness please be provided with a text marker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, can you please inform the Trial Chamber what you can see on the photograph in front of you on the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: You can see most of Guca Gora. You can't see Glavice, and you can't see the area around the school and also the area towards Volici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, Mr. Radic, please on the hard copy on your left side encircle the houses you have seen being burnt down after the attack on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Only on the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of June and later on. I'm only referring to houses you have seen yourself being burnt down.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, maybe it would be useful if the witness also told us where he was standing with his binoculars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, please first finish marking the houses, and afterwards would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: First you want me to put circles around the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks] I apologise. A part of the village is missing. One part towards the school and the other part towards Glavice; those two parts are missing in this photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, once you are finished, can you please put the photograph on the ELMO to your left side.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please, in addition, identify the houses you have seen been burnt down on the 8th of June, 1993, by writing the number "1" on the right-hand side of the circle, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The 8th of June, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 8th of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, the witness Radic has encircled the houses he has seen being burnt down after the attack at Guca Gora on the 8th of June, 1993, by encircling the houses; he has also identified the houses which were burnt down on 8 June 1993 by marking such houses in addition with the number "1." Mr. Radic, I'm coming back to the question which was asked by the Presiding Judge. Where were you standing at the time you have seen these houses you just marked being destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, I was in Nova Bila. And from Nova Bila, from the building where the headquarters of the Frankopan Brigade was, I saw the three houses that were set on fire sometime in the late afternoon, the houses that I marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you standing on the 12th and the 13th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was in Cifluk village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you in a position, Mr. Radic, to also identify the houses which were burnt or otherwise destroyed on the 12th and 13th of June, 1993, by adding to the circle the number "2"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: They are not in this photo. Those were in Glavice. Jakica Rajic, Tomo Rajic, and Stipica Rajic's houses were at the entrance to Guca Gora from the direction of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many houses, to your knowledge and from what you have seen yourself, were burnt down or otherwise destroyed on the 12th and 13th of June in the areas you just mentioned and which are not on the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Two houses were set on fire. They were at the very entrance to the village -- and two cow sheds, so four buildings altogether. And at the very entrance to the village, there was Stipo Rajic's house. And the first two houses belonged to Jakica and Tomo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, can you please again sign and date the photograph in front of you. Today is the 26th of February, 2004.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, again, I insist. He hasn't answered to the question of the Chamber. Where is Nova Bila? Is it to the right, to the left? Where is Nova Bila in respect of this photo? Can the witness please answer the Judge's question. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In respect of the photo, you had your binoculars and you were observing. From Nova Bila, where is Nova Bila in respect of this photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the centre of Guca Gora village, and to the south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. So you were in the south and through the binoculars you could see what was going on in Guca Gora. What was the distance between the locality and where you were standing with binoculars? How far was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 8th of June, when we were in Nova Bila, we could see the church and parish and we could see the three houses that were on fire. We could see with our naked eye which houses were on fire on that day. We had a direct line of vision, even without binoculars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show these three houses in the photo. Which are the three houses that you are now referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Danica Lujanovic's house, Ivka Neimarevic's house and Nikola Matkovic's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If I understand you well, you were in the south of the photo. And what was the distance between you and these three houses, 1 kilometre, 2 kilometres, 100 metres? What was the distance between these three houses and the place where you were standing with your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the crow flies? You mean as the crow flies? It was about 2 or 2 and a half kilometres, the distance between that area and Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the binoculars allowed you to see the place that was about 2 kilometres away; am I right in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These three houses, we could see them with our naked eye. With our naked eye, we could see these three houses burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Yes. And you also said that your house had been set on fire on the day when you were wounded. Your house, is your house in the photo or is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where is it? Can you show it to us? Can you show your house to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is here, at the place that you're showing us. Maybe the witness could mark it with a number. We have to be precise. When we're asking you questions, we want to be absolutely clear on things. We don't want to just have an approximation. Put a sign next to your house so as to show us where your house was. Can you put a sign, some sort of a symbol next to your house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I make a suggestion? The witness has been shown the map, Prosecution Exhibit P72, earlier on in the today's proceedings. The witness may be able to identify the location he's referring to as Nova Bila on this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, please have a look at the map. I think it's to your left side. Can you please identify the location you are referring to as Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please encircle the location Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For the transcript, the witness has identified Nova Bila on the map Prosecution Exhibit 72. Can the map please be shown to all participants. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, can you please again put the photograph on the ELMO, please. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to actually identify the marking you made in respect to your own house. Can you please fill in the black circle completely in black and write down "this is my own house."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read out, Mr. Radic, what you have written on the photograph. Unfortunately, I can't read the Croatian language.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: "This is my house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to tender this photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please give me an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next exhibit number is P73.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P73. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at the request of my learned friend, the witness first encircled his house and then blackened that area. Before that, he marked the houses which were burnt down by the end of June. Now we see that this place was blackened, although the witness said his house was set on fire on the 24th of December. So can we make a distinction. First there was a circle and now this is black. So can we make a distinction in order to know that this happened in some other period, that it didn't happen in June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he has indicated that his house was set on fire not in June but on 24th of December, 1993. So we are all clear that his house was set on fire on the 24th of December, there's no ambiguity. And also, he put words "this is my house" next to this blackened area. And we are clear, and you may rust assured that we will be able to distinguish between what happened in June and what happened subsequently in December. Mr. Withopf, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. This actually concludes the Prosecution's examination-in-chief. Thank you very much, Mr. Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, there was just something I would like to clarify before I let the Defence take the floor. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you were part of a medical unit and you said that you were its coordinator or you were in charge of this small medical unit. What sort of qualifications do you have? What sort of medical qualifications do you have? Are you a stretcher bearer, a nurse, doctor? What was your exact function within this medical unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I am a medical technician by profession, but I also served in the medical corps in the former JNA. After the war, I worked in the clinic in Travnik, in the emergency ward, so I was ready and prepared to prepare a field clinic. I was the commander of the medical unit within the brigade. My duties involved establishing field -- regional clinics in villages. These were small medical units which were to serve in case there were wounded who passed through. I had two or three people who would provide first aid in the field until the wounded were then transported to the hospital in Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we can conclude that you had logistical skills. Your contribution consisted of helping these units. You didn't have any medical functions. You didn't give anyone injections. You didn't give anyone cardiac massage. So you didn't have any particular medical qualifications. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. No. I'm a medical technician. I know how to provide basic first aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told us that sometimes you would call Dr. Suad Trskic, who was in the BH. You wanted to agree how to locate the wounded. When you phoned him -- when you called him, was it over the phone or was it over the radio?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, you have misunderstood me. Dr. Suad Trkic -- not Trskic but Trkic -- was a member of the BH army. He was deployed in Rudnik where the command was located. There used to be a clinic there. The Travnik health centre used to be there. Suad Trkic and I know each other from work because I worked in the health clinic in Travnik. We knew each other personally. Whenever we communicated, it was through our command, through the Frankopan Brigade and the 316th Mountain Brigade. So I would get into my vehicle, pass by the command, and consult him as to what should be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We thought that you would call him, but now you're saying that you would go through the military command; is that correct? You didn't get him on the phone; it was your military command. Is that correct? And my very last question - and we won't have any further questions for you, at least not as far as the Judges are concerned - you said a while ago that when there was looting, there were Muslim women, that's what you said. So these Muslim women, in your opinion, were they civilians or were they soldiers? On the basis of what you were able to see, what could you say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: They were civilians. The Muslim women were civilians. And what I saw through the binoculars, I saw Muslim women wearing baggy trousers, and I saw men - one, two, or three men, it depended - some only had the upper part of their uniform and some had a complete uniform on, whereas others were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'll turn to the Defence now for their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Radic. My name is Edina Residovic, and I represent General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll be asking you a number of questions relating to your testimony before this Trial Chamber. You said that you were born and lived in Guca Gora, in the municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say, Mr. Radic, that in March 1992 you were already mobilised into the Travnik Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zvonko Baja, who worked in the Territorial Defence, brought me a piece of paper and asked me to become a member of the Territorial Defence. That was during that period, during the first ten days. When I signed that, it meant that there would be a unit there and we could remain in our village if something worse happened than a Serb attack; it meant that we could be deployed up there. But in the following ten days, the situation changed completely and Territorial Defence no longer existed in the territory of Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. According to your testimony, on the 8th of April, 1992, you joined the HVO and pledged your allegiance to the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The task you were assigned by your brigade or unit, by the Travnik HVO Brigade, was to organise a field clinic in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While performing your duties, you were able to observe that in the second half of 1992 and at the beginning of 1993 in the territory of Travnik but also in the wider area of Guca Gora a large number of refugees started arriving.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In response to a question from my learned colleague, you said that many refugees arrived from Krajina, from Jajce, and from other parts of Western and Northwestern Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people you met and saw arrived there without any possessions, as they had been expelled from their houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, not all of them. Some of them were carrying weapons too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about property.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as property is concerned, yes, they didn't have anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the fall of Jajce, when the Serbian forces took the positions defended by the BH army and the HVO, the inhabitants of Jajce, as well as the defenders of Jajce, arrived in that area too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among those refugees, there were individuals and groups who carried weapons, who could be seen carrying weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, this was more the case for groups than for individuals. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1993, some of those people joined the BH army. They joined certain units in the BH army. But they could still be seen in the general area. They were unorganised or they were -- they organised themselves.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they joined the BH army immediately, but -- what else did you ask me about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These groups could be seen carrying weapons, and they would move around the area that you are familiar with.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time, at the beginning of 1993, the BH army, which was being founded, and the HVO didn't really have the uniforms of a normal, regular army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, they would all wear whatever they had. Some people had complete uniforms, but others had combined uniforms. They would wear parts of a uniform and their own clothes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, some people -- many people who could obtain uniforms, even if they weren't members of the HVO and the BH army, would put on parts of such uniforms because it was the fashion to wear a uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. It wouldn't be correct to say that it was the fashion to wear a camouflage uniform unless you were a member of some unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, tell me, please: In 1993 - since a while ago you said that you were able to listen to Radio Travnik - you heard over the radio and via the media that in other areas not far from Guca Gora there were armed conflicts between the army and the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993, did you hear through the media and in other ways that in the area and the vicinity of Guca Gora, in Vitez, for example, or in other areas, there were armed conflicts that broke out between the HVO and the BH army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, look, on the 8th of June, Nadja Ridzic, it was said that the BH army had expelled the Croatian extremists -- HVO extremists from Guca Gora and they were appealing to the population to return to their houses. They said they would protect them. Am I an extremist for having been expelled with my parents? Am I an extremist for this reason, and the other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as far as Vitez is concerned --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, Guca Gora and that area up there remained silent. There was no fighting while there was fighting in Travnik and Vitez. There were older people there who kept their word until the foreigners arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I said we'd turn to the 8th of June, but do you know -- are you aware of the fact that there was a conflict in Busovaca before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of a massacre in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as the massacre in Ahmici is concerned, we knew that there was fighting. But believe me, no one in Guca Gora knew about a massacre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said that there was a road passing through Guca Gora that linked up Travnik and Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in May 1993 the army had to use that road in order to get from Travnik to Zenica or from Zenica to Travnik? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, the normal road through Vitez and Busovaca, through the Lasva Valley, could not be used by the BH army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that. That road, the one you have just mentioned, about that road we got information from the command of the Travnik Brigade. For the sake of the Travnik-Zenica road, we were told that the command of the army and the HVO had agreed that a corridor between Travnik, Guca Gora, Maljine, Han Bila and Zenica would be used. We didn't know anything else about that corridor, apart from an agreement between the BH army and the HVO in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the centre of Guca Gora, the HVO held a checkpoint which is where people passing through would be checked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: That checkpoint was established after a checkpoint in Mosor had been established. So this was just a response to the establishment of a checkpoint in Mosor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware of the fact that on that road from Travnik to Zenica, not far from Guca Gora and in the direction of Travnik, on the 2nd of June the commander of the operative group Krajina, Mehmed Alagic, was stopped and disarmed and only when Commander Blaskic intervened and the international forces he was released? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I heard about that, but that -- something happened before that event. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at the checkpoint in Guca Gora four buses were stopped, buses transporting army members to positions facing the Serbian forces on Turbe?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were stopped because we had enough of all of that. There were a lot of troops from Zenica going through Guca Gora and those buses would take people to Mosor and onwards to Turbe. When the shift would return, two to three buses would return. One bus or lorry transporting troops would disappear and just didn't return. We were afraid that troops were being deployed in our part of the territory and the army and HVO covered Mosor. We were afraid of this. We were afraid that these people being transported from Zenica were being transported to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that on that road on a number of occasions the transport of the sick from Travnik to the Bolnica in Zenica was prevented?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the medical corps, and when someone was passing through from Travnik -- and everyone knew that I was in Guca Gora -- they would come to the checkpoint, they would call me, and they would then be sent on. So that is how they also enabled me to pass through Mosor and Radojcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your company that was previously part of the Travnik Brigade was reorganised and became part of the Frankopan Brigade in 1993. You said that that was on the 1st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The command of the brigade, as you said, up until the end of May or the 30th of May, which is what my learned colleague pointed out, the command was located in the old building within the monastery in Guca Gora; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Within the monastery in Guca Gora, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, the command left. It was moved to Nova Bila. And as for the old building, the communications centre remained there and the operations centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Just one person, a signalman stayed on and he had a radio set, and there was also an operations man affiliated with the brigade. He was a resident of Guca Gora. Two men only stayed on in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I move on, I would like to show you the map that you have already been presented by the Prosecution, but I'm going to give you a clean copy because I would like you to mark certain places that you have spoken about. I am going to ask you some questions about this map. On the ELMO now we can see the map. I believe that before we actually put it on the ELMO I would like you to show the place where Guca Gora is and mark it by number "1."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to put a circle around it and number "1"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, number "1."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put number "2" next to Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place where you left on the 8th of June, when you left Guca Gora. And then put number "3" next to Cifluk. Cifluk is the place where the separation line was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: My learned colleague just stated that Nova Bila was the place the witness left for on the 8th of June. The witness has repeatedly said that he left to the village of Cifluk on the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Maybe we have misunderstood each other. The witness is going to tell us. He told us that on the 8th of June he was watching three houses burning from Nova Bila. And to your question, Mr. President, he has repeated it. I may have heard him wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, with some of the troops and some civilians, we withdrew to Cifluk. We were digging ourselves up all day long. And sometime late in the afternoon I went to the headquarters, which is in Nova Bila, and from the headquarters late in the afternoon or in the early evening I saw the three houses burning. So it's on the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly how I understood you, but my learned friend had an objection, and we just wanted your clarification. We've had it now. So in the evening on the 8th of June you arrived in Nova Bila. And I've asked you to put a number "3" next to "Nova Bila."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, you said number "2."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, number "2." And now can you please put number "3" next to Cifluk.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also mentioned that you passed by Sarici village; however, I can't see this village in the map. If you know where it is, can you put "X" and "S" next to this village.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I've just put number "3" here. Can I put "X" over this number "3" and can I put number "3" on the other side?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: So I'm putting "X" and "S."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the record, how did you mark Sarici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I marked it with an "X" and with a "S."
