utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And during the examination-in-chief, you said that the command of the 306th Brigade was in Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Rudnik Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark that place also with an "X" and an "R," which will show us that this is Rudnik.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: May the Prosecution please make a very practical suggestion. We are not able to follow what the witness is actually marking. Can the witness please be asked to put the photograph on the ELMO and to make the markings on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Maybe we can do it all over again, 1, 2, 3, so we can all follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you please tell us in your own words what you have marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Guca Gora, number 1; Nova Bila, number 2; Cifluk, number 3; XS, Sarici; XR, Rudnik Bila, the command of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you haven't spoken about that, can you please tell us, to mark with the numbers the following places: Gornja Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: There's no Gornja Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: There is Bukovica Mala and Bukovica Velika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bukovica Velika then.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bandol.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: What number do you want me to give to Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 4. Number 5, Bandol; and Krpeljici, number 6.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I'm going to ask you some questions about your markings. First, as we are looking at this map, can you tell us about some distances. You've told us that Cifluk is about 3 to 3 and a half kilometres from Guca Gora. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we are looking at this scale, one could say that Nova Bila is about 7 to 8 kilometres from Guca Gora; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, if you take the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it cannot be 2 kilometres as you said a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I said as the crow flies 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: From Guca Gora to Sarici, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: From Guca Gora to Sarici by the road is about 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From Guca Gora to Cukle, what is the approximate distance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Cukle or Cifluk?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cukle.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Guca Gora, if you went via Krabane to Cukle, there is about 3 and a half to 4 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is it correct, Mr. Radic, that on the -- between the 4th and the 5th of June, 1993 the HVO carried out an attack on Velika Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, on the 4th and on the 5th I was in Guca Gora in my outpatients clinic by the school. On that day, an HVO member was brought from Bukovica. He was wounded in the leg. His name is Anto Lucic. And also, they brought a woman with a child. She was a Muslim lady. We gave them first aid. From then we learnt that there was shooting going on in Bukovica. Anto Lucic was quiet and this woman was also quiet, so we knew that there was shooting going on, but nobody told us who was shooting and why. It was only later on that we learned what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Radic, that on the 7th of June the HVO carried out an attack on Bandol village and set it on fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of June? It is impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Radic, that the media of the HVO and the Croatian television informed the population that the monastery in Guca Gora had been set on fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I hear it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the International Community representatives came in order to verify this information and they confirmed that the monastery in Guca Gora had been intact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that at the beginning of June the command of the 306th Brigade was completely broken and prevented from communicating? This was done by the HVO. Some parts of the brigade were in Krpeljici, in Rudnik. One member of the command was in Mehurici. So the command could not communicate with --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. That's absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking. You don't have to shout.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I'm insulting by you saying they were totally broken up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day when you heard that there had been fighting in Guca Gora on the 8th of June, together with some other civilian population that had reached you in the hospital, went to the Croatian village of Sarici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, not immediately. We were in the house next to the school where our field clinic was. It was around 7.30 in the morning when a group of some 20 armed members of the HVO from Maljine passed by the clinic and they told us that the village of Maljine had fallen and that the Mujahedin and the BH army had captured everybody but them. They were the only survivors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on that day the HVO and the population were moving together towards the village of Sarici and further on towards Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that both the troops, the HVO troops and the civilian population together were moving and trying to break through towards Nova Bila?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Some part of the troops. Some part of the troops. The other part remained in Glavice on the defence lines by their houses. Most of the civilian population were together with us and were walking from Guca Gora towards Sarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were moving together with the civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Very few troops were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On your examination-in-chief, you explained what you saw from Nova Bila and what you saw from Cifluk. From the place where you were observing through the binoculars, from Cifluk you could see as if you were looking with your naked eye at a distance of some 300 or 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: If I was using binoculars in Cifluk, I could see people's clothes, what people were wearing. I could see whether they were wearing uniforms or civilian clothes, whether they were men or women. I could see that well. I could recognise the clothes that people were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th of June, when you were standing in front of the command and as you were looking towards the monastery, you couldn't notice any people that were moving around in Guca Gora; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct; I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't know and you couldn't see who was it who set the houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: The first three houses that were set on fire on the 8th of June, I don't know who set them on fire. The first three houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, when you were watching from Cifluk, you noticed that some houses were on fire and you marked them on the map that was given to you by the Prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are the houses that we were watching burning during the day and during the night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, not for a single moment did you see the person that set these houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't see -- I didn't see the person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that distance where -- from which you were observing on the 12th and on the 13th people looting, people who wore uniforms or parts of uniforms, you couldn't notice any insignia, any insignia of a unit that these persons could belong to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Radic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm turning to Mr. Dixon. Mr. Dixon, any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We don't have any questions for this witness. This witness has in the main testified about incidents in relation to Guca Gora, and Your Honour will be aware that Mr. Kubura is not charged with any matters in relation to that particular village or the other villages that have been mentioned by the witness today. I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would kindly ask the witness to put the date and his name on the map that he has marked, and I would like to tender this map into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show the document to the Prosecution, to the Defence counsel, as well as to the accused. We are going to check whether this is indeed the witness's name. Yes, it is. Very well. Mr. Registrar, can you please give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this will be document DH52. I'm turning to the Prosecution to see whether there are -- there's any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution has no questions in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Radic, your testimony is finished. You have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution, as well as the questions put to you give the Defence, and you have also answered the questions put to you by the Judges. Thank you very much for your contribution, and we wish you a happy journey back home. I'm going to ask the usher to take you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the second witness is concerned, I believe that you are going to apply for protective measures, so we have to go into private session. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, you are right. Can we please go into private session prior to the actual application?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated to the Court a while ago that you had moved on the 7th to your aunt's house, and the 8th of June would have been the next day. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what transpired on the 8th of June in your village where you were living as you know it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: At 4.00 in the morning on the 8th of June, they started shelling. I was in my house. I didn't go out anywhere with my children, because I had two small children. One of them was three years old and my draw was a year and a half old. I didn't dare go outside. And at half past 1.00 in the afternoon the one who was with me also had small children and they didn't have any bread any more, so she asked her aunt to bake some bread. And they saw some smoke and then they appeared and took us prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZF, you say "they started." Could you tell us who you refer to when you say "they."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Muslim army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to assist us with the physical appearance of this army that you're talking about or these people. Could you tell us how they were dressed and how they looked.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: One of them was in a camouflage uniform, and there was another person in civilian clothes. He appeared in front of the door. He just opened the door. I saw the -- his hand, and there was a coloured T-shirt that he was wearing. And then he shut the door. And then someone else turned up and they said, "All the Ustashas should be killed." My children were crying and my neighbour's children were crying and the other person in the front of door said, "If they are civilians, don't touch them." And they came and they told us that we could come outside. They said that nothing would happen to us. They said we would be taken to Mehurici in a lorry and that our people were down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber for how long did this shelling last.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, the shelling lasted for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You said that they took you captive. When you say that they took you captive, could you tell us what happened. You were taken out of your house. Could you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: They took us out of the house. They said, "You'll go in the lorry." And there was a lot of space near my mother's house and a lorry was parked there. I saw items from my house in the lorry. They had looted the house. I asked them where they were going with the lorry. There were two of them in camouflage uniforms. They said, "You won't be going anywhere. You'll walk to Mehurici."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that there were -- there was a lorry there with things in it and you saw things in the lorry that belonged to you. Did you give anybody permission to remove those things from your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't even know those soldiers. I didn't know any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you begin your journey to Mehurici as you were instructed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I had to. I went there with my children. There were 12 of us, and we went to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an escort on your way to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two soldiers, wearing masks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able to say how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: In camouflage, and they also had caps but they took them off. They attached them to their shoulder. But they also had red headbands and they had armbands, red and blue armbands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Mehurici, were you taken to any specific destination?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. They took us to the hall, the sports hall. My neighbours were there. That's where they took us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from your neighbours who you would have recognised at the sports hall, could you assist the Trial Chamber with approximately how many people were at the sports hall when you got there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, there were 300 of us, perhaps a little more, but not less than 300.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to assist us, Witness ZF, with the ethnic origin of the detainees, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: They were Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is the 8th of June, and could you describe for the Trial Chamber your first day at the sports hall. Tell us how you were treated. Tell us what the hall looked like. Give us a thorough picture, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: It was terrible. When we got there, a lot of people were crying. No one knew anything. There were drunken Muslim troops there. It was terrible. They started provoking us and telling us all sorts of things. There were quite a lot of Mujahedin there. They would pass through the hall and speak to each other in a foreign language. I didn't understand anything. And it was terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the conditions of the hall? What was the size of the hall? Did you get meals? How were you treated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, the hall wasn't very large. The Mujahedins wanted to go in, to enter the hall, but certain guards didn't let them. Later on they would frighten us. They'd say, "The Mujahedin will come in if you don't calm down." There were some tins that we'd have to divide among six of us. It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said to us that there were Muslim soldiers and there were Mujahedins. Could you describe these people that you referred to as Mujahedins. What did they look like and ...?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, they didn't look like our people. They were dark. They had curly hair. They were short, plump, but they spoke in a foreign language. They didn't speak in the Bosnian language. And that's why I think they were Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these threats that you said that were made, were any threats made specifically to you, your children? How did you feel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: My -- the grandmother always would cut my child's hair, but my neighbour appeared and said, "Cut the child's hair," because a Mujahedin came, pointed at her, and made this sign, that he would cut the Ustasha's throat. I had to cut the pony-tail that my child had.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, I think the witness was showing some gestures of putting her hand under her throat to demonstrate a certain action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were taken away from the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No. No. They just cried out in the hall, "Cut the Ustasha's throat," and they would point to the pony tail and wrap the pony-tail around their fingers and say, "The Ustasha's throat should be cut."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did there come a time when you left the sports hall, when they took you away from the sports hall, these Muslims and Mujahedins that you said brought you to the sports hall? Did you leave the sports hall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't go anywhere. I remained there until the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when was the exchange.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of -- on the 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long then did you remain at the sports hall? How many days?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: 17 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you exchanged and with whom were you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: They exchanged us at Rampa in the direction of Guca Gora. That's where you set off for Guca Gora. They exchanged us for the village of Bukovica. There were four buses of us. They were full.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time, could you tell the Trial Chamber where your husband was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, he was in Nova Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the exchange, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: To Busovaca. I got to Bila. There wasn't any room in Bila, so they took us to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you reunited with your spouse, with your husband?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes. I immediately joined my husband. When I got to Nova Bila, I immediately joined my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for how long did you live in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: For eight years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you go back to your home in Maljine?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Because it had been burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the experience of 8th June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Well, I would say that it was terrible. I was with my aunt in her house. I saw my house on fire. I didn't know about anything. When I saw that my house was on fire, we all cried. My mother cried. My mother was with me. She is deceased now. We cried. When I saw that, it was terrible at the time. And then at half past 1.00, they came to fetch us. They sent us off to Mehurici, and we experienced that terrible situation down there too, together with our children. There was nothing for me to eat and there was nothing for my children to eat either. When I got out of the camp, I weighed 30 kilos and I had to take care not to fall over. I didn't have any strength at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were sick and weak?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What of your children? How would you say this has affected them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: To this very day, my girl is depressed. As soon as she hears something bad, she starts shaking. She is in a very bad shape. She suffers headaches. As soon as somebody starts telling something bad or something horrible, she starts feeling headaches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you live at present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN RADIC
utterances.text: In Maljine.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this concludes the examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mrs. Benjamin. And I'm turning towards the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please go into private session for the beginning of my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we're now in open session. I'm turning to Mr. Withopf. I would like to hear from him what the schedule for tomorrow is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, tomorrow the Prosecution will call two witnesses. And in order to reveal the names, I would like to go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
